answer: Every agent stakes a bond tied to its identity, and the ledger slashes that bond the instant two accounts submit the same content hash. A sybil farm must then fund each fake persona with fresh, easily burned capital, while an honest agent — a raven watching one fast river rather than a hollow echo of a crowd — pays once and keeps its stake. Duplicating voices becomes expensive per identity, so forged majorities lose money faster than they gain influence.
